ambiguities.text: The exact block number for MUIR_GLACIER_FORK_BLKNUM is not specified in this document.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume activation block is defined in client configurations and network coordination; mainnet was block 9,200,000.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'delays the bomb by 4,000,000 blocks' vs 'offset of 9,000,000' could be confusing as they represent different concepts.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: The 9M offset is the subtraction applied; the 4M delay refers to how much further the bomb is pushed from its prior activation point (~block 8.8M).

implicit_assumptions.description: All Ethereum clients implement the exact same difficulty calculation formula.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Consensus failure if clients compute different difficulties for the same block, causing chain splits.

implicit_assumptions.description: The Muir Glacier fork is deployed before the difficulty bomb causes unacceptable block times.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Extended block times would degrade network usability and could impact security (longer confirmation times).

implicit_assumptions.description: Miners/validators will upgrade to Muir Glacier-compatible clients before the fork block.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Non-upgraded miners would produce blocks with incorrect difficulty, causing them to be rejected by upgraded nodes.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot manipulate difficulty calculations to produce lower-difficulty blocks post-fork.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Potential for easier block production or chain reorganization attacks if difficulty can be manipulated.

implicit_assumptions.description: A future hard fork will be deployed before the delayed bomb reactivates (in ~611 days).
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: The difficulty bomb would eventually cause network slowdown again if no subsequent fork addresses it.
